articles.title: Iran’s security chief calls US response to deal conditions ‘inadequate’
articles.summary:
Iran’s security chief calls US response to deal conditions ‘inadequate’

Washington must clarify its position before talks on a possible agreement can advance, Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei says.

“The Americans have now responded to us. In their response, they have accepted some of our conditions, while others remain unclear,” the Supreme National Security Council secretary told the semi-official Tasnim news agency.

Rezaei described the US response as “inadequate”.

“We are no longer in the process of responding to the Americans,” he said. “They must clarify the issues that remain unclear to us,” he added.

The exchange follows President Donald Trump’s rejection late last month of an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days.

US Vice President JD Vance subsequently demanded a “meaningful” reduction in Iran’s uranium enrichment capacity as a condition for an agreement.

Iran’s security chief accuses Trump administration of oil smuggling near Oman
articles.summary:
Iran’s security chief accuses Trump administration of oil smuggling near Oman

Mohsen Rezaei has accused the Trump administration of recruiting “thugs” to smuggle oil through coastal waters off Oman.

Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary said the UAE military and the commander of US Central Command also participate in the operation, according to state-linked news agency ISNA.

Trump “claims every day that the Strait of Hormuz is open, but in response I say: ‘You are smuggling, but the strait is under Iranian control and we manage it,'” Rezaei said.

He said the operation relies on a handful of “small vessels to transfer oil to larger tankers”, adding that Iran attacks them “every night”.

articles.title: Iran security chief accuses Trump of ‘smuggling’ oil through Hormuz
articles.summary:
Iran security chief accuses Trump of ‘smuggling’ oil through Hormuz

Iran’s security chief claimed on Sunday that US President Donald Trump's adminitation hired “thugs” in the coastal waters of Oman to smuggle oil through the Iranian blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump “claims every day that the Strait of Hormuz is open, but in response I say: ‘You are smuggling, but the strait is under Iranian control and we manage it,'” Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei was quoted as saying by Iran's ISNA news agency.

Rezaei said that the smuggling operation involves the UAE military and the commander of US Central Command (Centcom) using a handful of “small vessels to transfer oil to larger tankers” and that Iran targets them “every night”.
